observation: Neuron-only Wwox deletion reduces OL maturation, myelinated axons and conduction
relation_hypothesised: Missing or distorted neuron-derived signal acts on wild-type OPCs (non-cell-autonomous)
possible_action: Bypass the signal pharmacologically instead of restoring WWOX
context: Mouse, neuron-specific conditional deletion, cortex and hippocampus; postnatal myelination
benefit_to_verify: Myelin maturation, sheath, conduction restored without WWOX
favourable_reason: OPCs retain WWOX yet fail to mature
unfavourable_or_alternative: Report itself: intrinsic contribution in patients not excluded; neuron-specific deletion may also alter circuit activity or other glia indirectly (not discussed)
discriminating_experiment: Deletion-site x drug factorial (Arm A vs Arm B)
reasoning_pattern: A phenotype appearing after deletion in cell type X is read as a lost signal from X to a genetically intact neighbour, hence bypassable

observation: WWOX loss hyperactivates GSK-3beta; GSK-3beta restrains OL differentiation in vivo in non-WWOX systems
relation_hypothesised: Hyperactive GSK-3beta in WWOX-null brain brakes OPC differentiation
context: Mouse; GSK-3beta data from Wwox-/- brain (seizures) and from postnatal wild-type brain and optic nerve (myelination); cell type of hyperactivation not specified
benefit_to_verify: Restored maturation and sheath in neuron-deletion mice; dual seizure and myelin benefit
measured_or_inferred_per_step: obs=measured (each half, separately); relation=inferred (join of two systems); action=speculative
favourable_reason: Convergent node; lithium anti-seizure already seen in Wwox-/-
unfavourable_or_alternative: Report: chain never closed in one study; GSK-3beta effects on myelin come from non-WWOX systems; lithium pleiotropic
discriminating_experiment: Neuron-deletion animals plus selective inhibitor, scoring OPC beta-catenin targets and maturation, confirming WWOX not restored
reasoning_pattern: A kinase de-repressed by gene loss in disease A and a known negative regulator of a process in system B are joined at the shared node

observation: Neuregulin raises NMDA currents in OL lineage and shifts myelination to activity-dependent mode
relation_hypothesised: WWOX-null E/I imbalance and impaired conduction degrade that activity-dependent cue
context: Neuron-OL co-culture or mouse (as cited); stage called adult by the report

unfavourable_or_alternative: Conflicts with Framing B; neuregulin/BDNF link to WWOX not shown
discriminating_experiment: Neuregulin/NMDA enhancement vs chemogenetic dampening in neuron-specific null cortex at fixed early window
reasoning_pattern: A signalling pathway known to carry neuron-to-glia information is nominated as the missing signal in a mutant

observation: Early development: higher neuronal activity reduces OL differentiation; WWOX-null cortex is hyperexcitable and hypomyelinated
relation_hypothesised: Excess early activity itself suppresses OPC differentiation, linking seizure and myelin arms
context: Mouse early postnatal cortex; AMPAR gating; WWOX data from null cortex
benefit_to_verify: Myelin improvement as a consequence of seizure control
favourable_reason: Inverted stage rule fits the disease window
unfavourable_or_alternative: Report flags conflict with PMID 24391468; correlation of hyperexcitability and hypomyelination in same animals is not causal
discriminating_experiment: Chemogenetic dampening vs neuregulin/NMDA enhancement at defined timepoint
reasoning_pattern: A stage-dependent rule from a normal-development study is transferred to a mutant and used to reverse the sign of the proposed cue

relation_hypothesised: OPC-intrinsic promyelinating drug bypasses any missing neuronal supply
context: Mouse Pdk1 icKO (as cited); also stroke model
benefit_to_verify: Maturation restored in Arm A; fails in nothing-specific Arm B

unfavourable_or_alternative: Rescue in a different genetic defect does not show a neuronal-signal bypass in WWOX
discriminating_experiment: Factorial with clemastine in Arm A and B
reasoning_pattern: A drug that rescues one genetic myelin defect is used as a mechanism-agnostic probe for another

observation: T3 raises mature OL and myelin without changing OPC markers (cuprizone) and rescues S-ketamine hypomyelination via PPARalpha

unfavourable_or_alternative: Rescue by T3 in a different model does not itself define the WWOX lesion stage
